samples.question: A pale sheet shows a long grey horizontal beam. One black triangle above the beam points down at a single place on it; that place is the pivot. Two stacks of identical small solid squares hang below the beam, one navy and one crimson, one on each side of the pivot. For each of those two stacks take the number of squares it contains and multiply it by the horizontal distance from the pivot to the middle of that stack's column. Olive squares, orange rings, orange bars and the grey ticks along the bottom edge are decoration and are never counted or measured. Which colour's stack gives the larger product, navy or crimson?
